steps.content: You lay the three photos before Hilda, urging her to look closely.
The first captures the moment Horne is handed a glass of red wine by a server, just as Huck steps into the frame to confront him. An argument is already brewing.
In the second photo, Horne's wine glass lies shattered. He dabs furiously at the stains on his clothes with a handkerchief while in a heated argument with Marlo.

The third photo shows Horne brazenly interrupting a conversation between Nolaine and another guest. He seems to be boasting, forcing Nolaine's attention onto him, while the two interrupted parties look on with clear annoyance.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: We all assumed these photos showed Horne with three different people. But we missed it: there's a fourth person in all of them.
The server in the first one, the one offering the handkerchief in the second, and the man talking to Nolaine before they were interrupted.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That's the fourth person we keep overlooking. Edward.
Hilda applauds, a look of genuine approval on her face.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Precisely. Edward is a master of presence. Unless you're actively looking for him, your eye simply slides right past.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: What led you to him?

options: I have a keen eye for detail.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Is that so? I wouldn't have imagined our "anomalous power expert" would have an intelligence contact. What a surprise.
Hilda's Trust +1
(Paths converge)

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Your conclusion matches my own. I'll have someone extend an invitation to Edward. We'll "inquire" about this matter. Thoroughly.
She draws herself upright, and when she speaks again, her tone is softer.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: I owe you an apology, ${PlayerName}. I doubted your identity... or perhaps, I still haven't entirely confirmed who you are.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: But your knowledge of the anomalous power is undeniably professional. And beyond that, you possess a sharp deductive sense. To pick Edward out from so little... I am impressed.
Though her words are praise, her demeanor rests in a space between suspicion and trust. The look in her eyes is one of open curiosity and confusion.
You remain unshaken, meeting her gaze directly and responding with calm assurance.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I was just doing my job. It's nothing like your plan—using yourself and the "Monolith" as bait, gathering every dangerous suspect in one place. I'd never have the nerve for something that bold.
At your words of praise, Hilda's gaze instinctively darts away.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Bold? DisCity runs inhumane experiments just for an edge, creating undead soldiers controlled by dangerous weapons... The mole sells our secrets and betrays the city-state, heedless of the consequences.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Compared to them, my methods are the picture of reason.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: This isn't for me. It's for the people we've lost... and for the city-state's future. That is why I'm willing to be a piece on the board, to draw out the mole and sever this threat.
Her voice is cold and resolute, the words meant as much for herself as for you.
Just then, a sudden, urgent pounding at the door shatters the moment.

steps.speaker: Marlo
steps.content: Hilda, we've got a problem. Edward's gone. Vanished. We've turned the whole damn manor upside down; he's not here.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: What?
[Scene Change: Main Hall]
You hurry after Marlo into the main hall, where the others have already reconvened. He retrieves several items from a table and presents them to Hilda.

steps.speaker: Marlo
steps.content: We found this stuff in an empty room. Looks like he ditched anything that would've slowed him down.
You see a miniature recording device, cleverly disguised as a cigarette box, its model nearly identical to the one Horne was given.

Beside it lies an open personnel file, its contents fanned out across the table. With a jolt, you recognize them. These are the dossiers on everyone present, the very files you had asked Edward to compile upon your arrival at the manor. He actually followed through.

steps.speaker: Marlo
steps.content: No one on the perimeter saw a thing. The place is surrounded by forest and cliffs, and with this rain causing flash floods... he couldn't possibly get out. He's still here, somewhere.

steps.speaker: Marlo
steps.content: Let's get more people and sweep the grounds. We'll find him.
The others all nod, their faces set in determined lines. They're now convinced Edward is the mole, and that flushing him out is the only way this nerve-wracking gathering ends.
With that, you also join the search party.
The manor looms around you. Where do you begin?

steps.speaker: Option
options: The third-floor study where the files were found
The terrace garden with an open view

steps.content: The room is as the previous search left it, a storm of scattered papers and overturned pens. Among the chaos, you spot a stack of blank paper, presumably left behind by Edward.
There are no more clues here. You should look elsewhere.
A cold rain sheets across the terrace. You sweep the area thoroughly, only to find nothing but the grim weather.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...I should go back.
The place is a wreck. You step in and freeze. You're not alone. You can sense another person breathing.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Haha... Of course it's you, ${PlayerName}. I had a feeling you'd be the one to find me.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Sigh... You know, a few other groups already swept through here. None of them even glanced my way. I was starting to get bored.
Peering into the darkness, you make out a figure slouched against the wall, idly toying with a small object in hand.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Let's not move, alright? I've got a gun. Not really my weapon of choice, so it's a bit unpredictable. I just... want to talk before I go.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Tell me, did you find the documents I left for you?
You nod toward the direction of the voice.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Good. I made sure Hilda's was the most comprehensive. I left it all for you.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: ${PlayerName}, I don't know who you really are... but I would genuinely enjoy working with you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What are you talking about? I don't understand.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Heh, it's okay. I get it. Don't worry, your secret's safe with me. In fact, I want to help you.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: You know, with my disposition, I'm only fit to be a spy... but I've always hated skulking in the shadows. Doing something for you, though... that was different. It felt good.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: You're the only one who actually saw me. You paid attention, you cared. Having a superior like you... it would mean a lot to me.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: I was just unlucky... DisCity caught me in a bad spot. To stay alive, I had to feed them intel from the metropoles, including some about Monolith... And, well, I guess Hilda finally figured it out.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Ever wonder why someone like me was even invited to a meeting like this? I'm a decent spy, but I know nothing about cipher machines. She just wanted to smoke me out.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: I suppose in her mind, it doesn't matter who the mole is. If she eliminates everyone, she gets the mole too, right?

options: If you tell me who the mole is, I can put in a word for you.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: That? Nothing personal. The mole just told me to pick the weakest-looking target and test the waters.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: That man was full of holes. Getting leverage on him was almost too easy.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: ${PlayerName}, I think you're the one who's not seeing things clearly. You don't understand her at all... Let me give you some advice: don't pin your hopes on her. That woman's heart belongs entirely to the city-state. There's no room for anything else.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: As for the "mole," you should stop trying to catch them. You won't be able to.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Well, friend... this is the path I chose. I ran out of options a long time ago. At least I got to have this last chat with you... <color=#fb9259>I've left something for you. Whether it's useful or not... that'll be up to you.</color>
He raises the gun and points it at his own head.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Well, we've talked long enough... It's probably time to... say goodbye.
A gunshot rings out, and Edward collapses. On his lifeless face, there is no pain or fear, only an inexplicable, profound look of satisfaction.
For a spy who never chose his life, this final, defiant act may have been one of the few decisions that were truly his own.
Minutes later, Hilda bursts into the cellar. Her eyes instantly find Edward's body, then you, standing over him.
Her lips press into a thin, hard line. Without a word, she strides to your side and, with a leather-clad thumb, gently wipes the blood from your cheek.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Tell me what happened.
